newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Braced for a weaker market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Braced for a weaker market.

text.p: Trading of regional barrels for March and Middle East crudes for April are expected to start in earnest this week, with most players braced for weaker premiums.
Singapore refineries, with a capacity of around 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd), are maintaining run cuts of around 90,000 bpd.
Japanese and South Korean refiners will be in the midst of maintenance checks, further limiting demand as the market moves into a traditionally weaker part of the trading year.
Traders said regionally, they expect the medium and heavy sweet grades to come under most pressure.

Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina is planning a 38-day shutdown of the 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery from this coming weekend for maintenance, which will release more benchmark Minas crude onto the spot market.
Pertamina's export allocations are expected to come out on Monday or Tuesday, which will give the market an idea of how much crude will be floating on the spot market.
A weaker tone for Minas will knock similar grades such as Widuri and Cinta, although one exporter said he only expected a couple of Widuri cargoes to be available for March trading.
But traders said West African imports are also heading East, acting as a further depressant on the market.
They said they expected March Minas to trade initially between ICP +50/70 cents. For most of February it traded above ICP +$1.00, although drifted to last trade for February at ICP +75 cents.
"It's not going to be as good as January or February, but we were spoiled then," one trader said of the forthcoming March market.

However, light sweet grades were showing more strength. Unexpected demand from a major in New Zealand tightened the Tapis market and the loss of production from Australia's Cossack market has further underpinned the grade.
Operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Friday production at Cossack has been halved to 40,000 bpd and the cut could be in place until mid-March.
An Australian producer has already sold its March availabilities of three light sweet cargoes outside Australia.
"Naphtha rich crudes will be supported as naphtha is relatively strong against other products. But there are still question marks over gas oil, despite recent Tapis deals," said one trader.
Middle East crudes face a similarly bleak outlook and traders are increasingly talking of the lighter ADNOC grades slipping to a discount.
"The market perhaps might run negative for April. ADNOC grades will be particularly hit because the differentials remain high," one buyer said.
ADNOC differentials to benchmark Dubai crude only came in a few cents per barrel when January official selling prices (OSP) were announced.
Traders use the differential as a basis for assessing crude values.
Although the OSPs reflect barrels traded for lifting in January, traders said they should also have a forward element because the market's psychology was now moving forward to trade April crude.
"It was a slap in the face for the buyer," the buyer said of the OSPs.
Traders said Oman crude will face similar problems in attracting buyers. Its differential to Dubai widened for April to $1.14 per barrel from $1.04 during March.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
